```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

The outer folds of a nested run do not depend on one another, so they can
run at the same time. The nested functions send them to
[mirai](https://mirai.r-lib.org/) daemons (separate R processes) when two
or more are connected, and run them one after another otherwise.

```{r deps, include = FALSE}
needed <- c("tidymodels", "mirai", "ranger")
missing_pkgs <- needed[
  !vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
has_deps <- length(missing_pkgs) == 0L
```

```{r deps-notice, eval = !has_deps, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat(
  "This page attaches the **tidymodels** packages, runs the outer loop on",
  "**mirai** daemons and fits random forests with the **ranger** package.",
  if (length(missing_pkgs) == 1L) {
    sprintf("The **%s** package is not installed here,", missing_pkgs)
  } else {
    sprintf(
      "The **%s** packages are not installed here,",
      paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = "** and **")
    )
  },
  "so the rest of this page has been skipped. Install",
  if (length(missing_pkgs) == 1L) "it" else "them",
  "and rebuild to see it.\n"
)

knitr::knit_exit()
```

```{r libraries, message = FALSE}
library(tidymodels)
library(nestedtune)
```

## The setup

We reuse the design, the random forest and the grid from
`vignette("nested-cv")`.

```{r design}
set.seed(1)

folds <- nested_resamples(
  mtcars,
  outside = vfold_cv(v = 5),
  inside = vfold_cv(v = 5)
)

rf <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 500) |>
  set_engine("ranger") |>
  set_mode("regression")

wf <- workflow(mpg ~ ., rf)

grid <- expand.grid(mtry = c(2L, 5L, 8L), min_n = c(2L, 10L))
```

## Running in parallel

We start a pool of two daemons with `mirai::daemons()`. The call to
`nested_tune_grid()` does not change.

```{r run-parallel}
mirai::daemons(2)

set.seed(2)
par_res <- nested_tune_grid(wf, folds, grid = grid)

par_res
```

Each fold's inner tuning runs serially on its daemon, so the two loops do
not compete for cores. The first call after starting a pool is slower,
because each daemon loads the packages the workflow needs.

`mirai::daemons(0)` stops the pool, and the same call then runs serially.

```{r daemons-stop}
mirai::daemons(0)
```

## The same result

The fold seeds are drawn before any fold is sent out, so one seed gives
one result serially and in parallel, as `?nested_tune_grid` explains.

```{r identity}
set.seed(2)
ser_res <- nested_tune_grid(wf, folds, grid = grid)

c(
  metrics = identical(par_res$.metrics, ser_res$.metrics),
  selected = identical(par_res$.selected, ser_res$.selected)
)
```

## When a pool pays

On `mtcars` each fold takes a fraction of a second, so starting two
daemons costs more than it saves. A pool pays when the folds are
expensive: more data, a bigger grid, a slower engine or a costly recipe.
